gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Commanding and a bit vintage, Woodgod pushes its tall lowercase almost up to the capitals. Noto Sans Hanunoo fills the line with open-ended sans-serif letters that stay contemporary and easy to follow over a long passage.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew reads modern and businesslike, its big midsection leaving wide gaps where curves meet stems. Woodgod does its best work shouting from the top with vintage weight, while Noto Sans Hebrew is happiest carrying the plain sans text underneath.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-hk: Noto Sans HK sets large lowercase forms with brush ends that lift away before each curve closes, tidy and clean. Woodgod's vintage authority is the real draw.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Bold vintage swagger meets friendly plain sans. Woodgod's tall lowercase nearly touches its capitals, and Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic echoes that short step with c shapes whose ends point apart like open pincers.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-inscript: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is clean and wide-eyed. Its deep middle band and open e and a shapes make it forgiving at modest sizes, so Woodgod can take the commanding vintage spotlight alone.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-jp: Commanding is how Woodgod looks, vintage and tall in the lowercase. Noto Sans JP, with its very tall x-height and sweeping curves, would crowd that effect if the heading shrank or the sans body grew large.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi fills each line with big lowercase forms. Beneath Woodgod's vintage, commanding heading it reads smooth and contemporary, with the e's open channel keeping a longer page moving along.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Friendly modern text under a vintage shout. Woodgod is best at commanding attention with its wide-channelled bowls, and Noto Sans Kannada is best at carrying words with its gentle capital bump and wide-open s curves.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Noto Sans Kayah Li reads clean, with capitals barely taller than lowercase. Under Woodgod's vintage heading, a long stretch of text flows smoothly, the lifted brush ends keeping each curve open.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kharosht: Vintage muscle meets a friendly, dark-striped text. Woodgod's commanding tall lowercase gets a worthy partner in Noto Sans Kharoshthi, whose curves never close back on themselves, making the pair strikingly approachable.
